intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Snorkeling & Cliff Walk
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches with crystal-clear waters ideal for snorkeling among rock arches and sea caves. The coastal cliff walk offers breathtaking views and is easily accessible from Lagoa town, keeping you close to central accommodation hubs. Best enjoyed after an early afternoon flight arrival, making it a perfect Day 1 activity.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood. Sessions run in the afternoon and the venue is within 10 minutes of major hotel clusters in Carvoeiro and Armação de Pêra, eliminating long transfers.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave and surrounding grottos on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours depart at sunrise for calm waters and smaller crowds. The departure point is centrally located, making it accessible from hotels in Carvoeiro or Armação de Pêra within a short drive.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Wine Trail
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and stroll through the historic old town, stopping at local wine bars and tavernas offering regional Algarve wines and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally positioned and reachable within 20 minutes from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels, making it an efficient cultural half-day excursion.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Picnic with Local Wines
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed evening on the long golden stretch of Meia Praia near Lagos, enjoying a curated picnic basket with local Algarve wines, regional cheeses, and smoked fish sourced from the Lagos market. This experience is self-guided and budget-friendly, wrapping up a full day perfectly. Lagos town center offers ample accommodation options right next to the beach.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer to Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed walk around Lagoa town centre. Explore the charming streets, visit the local market square, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Lagoa's main street and enjoy a casual first dinner at a local tasca (traditional Portuguese tavern). Pick up a bottle of local Algarve wine from a nearby supermarket to enjoy on your accommodation terrace.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport café upon landing — approx €3
meals.lunch: Quick bite at airport or roadside café during transfer — approx €8
meals.dinner: Tasca O Zé or similar local tavern in Lagoa town — grilled fish of the day with house wine — approx €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Transfer from Faro Airport to Lagoa takes approximately 40 minutes by bus (Eva Bus line) for around €5, or a shared taxi for €20–25. September weather in Algarve is warm and sunny, typically 25–28°C — perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most picturesque beaches near Lagoa. Walk down the cliffside steps to the golden sandy cove, swim in the crystal-clear Atlantic waters, and explore the dramatic rock formations along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Carvoeiro Boardwalk (Passadiço de Carvoeiro) — a free scenic wooden walkway carved into the cliffs offering stunning ocean views. Explore the sea caves and rock arches at Algar Seco, just a 20-minute walk from Carvoeiro village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for sunset drinks at a clifftop bar. Browse the small souvenir shops and enjoy the lively village atmosphere before heading back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa town — coffee, toast with local butter and jam — approx €4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) — bread, cheese, local ham, fruit — approx €6
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Carvoeiro village — piri-piri chicken or grilled sardines with salad and local wine — approx €14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Carvoeiro is approximately 5 km from Lagoa. Take a local bus (Vamus Algarve) for €2 each way or rent a bicycle for the day for around €10–12. Bring sunscreen, water, and a towel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Adega do Cantor winery near Lagoa — one of Algarve's most celebrated wineries, famously associated with Cliff Richard. Take a guided tour of the vineyard and wine cellar (approx €10–15 per person) and learn about the local Algarve wine production.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting session at Adega do Cantor sampling their Vida Nova and Aneto labels — red, white, and rosé wines made from local grape varieties. Purchase a bottle of local wine at cellar-door prices for a great budget souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Silves town (15 minutes from Lagoa) for dinner. Walk through the historic Moorish streets and enjoy the atmospheric old town at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Local café near Lagoa Boutique Stay — galão coffee and croissant — approx €3.50
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery café or nearby roadside café — soup, bread, and local cheese — approx €8
meals.dinner: Café Inglês restaurant in Silves — traditional Algarvian cuisine, cataplana de peixe (fish stew) — approx €15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Adega do Cantor tour in advance via their website. A taxi or rideshare to the winery costs approximately €8–10 each way. Silves is easily reached by train from Lagoa station for €2.30 each way — one of the best budget transport options in the region.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — explore the magnificent Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), a well-preserved Moorish fortress dating back to the 8th century. Entry costs €3 per person. Enjoy panoramic views over the terracotta rooftops and surrounding orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Silves Cathedral (Igreja da Sé) — free entry. Wander through Silves' cobblestone streets, browse the local artisan shops, and visit the Municipal Museum of Archaeology (€2 entry). Stop at the riverside promenade along the Arade River.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the evening passeio (evening stroll) with locals along Silves' main boulevard. Enjoy a leisurely dinner at a riverside restaurant before catching the train back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Padaria (bakery) in Lagoa — fresh bread roll with ham and orange juice — approx €3
meals.lunch: Local tasca in Silves old town — prato do dia (dish of the day) including soup, main, and dessert — approx €9–10
meals.dinner: Marisqueira (seafood restaurant) near Silves riverside — grilled sea bass with vegetables and local wine — approx €13–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Train from Lagoa to Silves runs regularly and costs €2.30 each way — highly recommended as a scenic and budget-friendly option. The castle is the highlight of the Algarve interior and should not be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia da Marinha — widely considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Portugal and all of Europe. Take a bus or taxi (approx 10 km from Lagoa) and spend the morning swimming among the golden limestone cliffs and sea arches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the sea caves and grottos accessible from Praia da Marinha by kayak. Rent a kayak from a local operator on the beach for approximately €15–20 per person for 2 hours. Paddle through the stunning arch formations and hidden sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Visit a local wine bar or adega in Lagoa town to sample regional wines by the glass at low prices.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — coffee and toast with local honey and butter — approx €3.50
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha — fresh grilled fish sandwich and local beer — approx €10
meals.dinner: Supermarket provisions and self-catering dinner at accommodation — fresh local bread, cheese, charcuterie, olives, and a bottle of Algarve rosé — approx €12 for two

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is accessed via a steep cliff path — wear sturdy shoes for the descent. The beach can get busy in September but is still manageable. Arrive before 10:30 AM to secure a good spot. Bring plenty of water as there are limited facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Portimão town (15 km from Lagoa) — explore the lively riverside market and waterfront promenade. Browse the Mercado Municipal de Portimão for fresh local produce, cheeses, smoked fish, and Algarve almonds at excellent prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu de Portimão (Portimão Museum) — housed in a former sardine canning factory, this award-winning museum tells the story of the local fishing and canning industry. Entry is €3 per person or free on the last Sunday of each month.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its sardine restaurants along the riverside. Enjoy a classic Algarvian sardine dinner at one of the many affordable grill restaurants along the Arade riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria in Lagoa — fresh pastries and coffee — approx €3
meals.lunch: Market lunch in Portimão — fresh local produce, bread, and olives bought at the market — approx €6–8
meals.dinner: Riverside sardine restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines with boiled potatoes and salad, house wine — approx €12–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Lagoa to Portimão runs frequently and costs approximately €2.50 each way. Portimão is also the gateway to Praia da Rocha — a large and popular beach resort just 2 km south of the town centre if you want to combine a beach visit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia da Rocha — Portimão's famous wide sandy beach backed by dramatic ochre-coloured cliffs. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing on one of the Algarve's largest and most iconic beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the clifftop promenade at Praia da Rocha with panoramic views over the beach. Visit the small Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry) — a 17th-century fortress at the river mouth with excellent views towards Ferragudo village across the Arade estuary.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short ferry across the Arade River to the charming village of Ferragudo (ferry approx €1.50 each way). Explore the picturesque fishing village, visit the local castle, and enjoy dinner at a traditional restaurant overlooking the estuary.

meals.breakfast: Café on Praia da Rocha promenade — coffee and pastel de nata — approx €3
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar on Praia da Rocha — grilled chicken pitta and local beer — approx €9
meals.dinner: Traditional restaurant in Ferragudo village — amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams) and grilled fish with local wine — approx €15–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is the halfway point of your trip — a great day to reflect on your Algarve experience so far. Ferragudo is one of the most authentic and unspoiled fishing villages in the Algarve and is far less touristy than Portimão or Carvoeiro.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day at Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (approximately 8 km from Lagoa). This highly regarded estate produces award-winning Algarve wines and offers guided tours and tastings from €12 per person. Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine theme with a visit to the Lagoa Wine Cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa) — one of the oldest and most important wine producers in the Algarve. Purchase local wines at cooperative prices — excellent value.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagoa town. Attend a local evening concert or cultural event if available (check the Câmara Municipal de Lagoa events calendar). Enjoy a nightcap of local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Self-catering at accommodation — local bread, fruit, and coffee — approx €4
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Quinta dos Vales winery café — local cheese and charcuterie board paired with wine — approx €12
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Lagoa — bifanas (pork sandwiches) or bacalhau (salt cod) with local wine — approx €12–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: A taxi or rideshare to Quinta dos Vales costs approximately €10–12 each way. Alternatively, rent a bicycle for the day to visit both the winery and the cooperative. September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may witness the grape harvest in action at the vineyards.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (approximately 25 km west of Lagoa). Explore the historic walled old town, including the Igreja de Santo António (€2 entry) and the Municipal Museum. Walk along the ancient town walls and visit the slave market memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the short walk from Lagos old town down to Praia Dona Ana — one of the most photographed beaches in Portugal, surrounded by extraordinary golden rock formations and sea arches. Swim and explore the rock pools.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' vibrant nightlife area — the town is famous for its lively bar scene. Enjoy happy hour drinks at one of the many bars in the old town before catching the last bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa before departure — coffee and toast — approx €3
meals.lunch: Mercado Municipal de Lagos — fresh fruit, local bread, and cheese from the market stalls — approx €6
meals.dinner: Traditional restaurant in Lagos old town — frango piri-piri (piri-piri chicken) with fries and salad — approx €12–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Lagoa to Lagos takes approximately 40 minutes and costs €3.50 each way. Buses run regularly throughout the day. Lagos is one of the most popular destinations in the Algarve — arrive early to beat the crowds at Praia Dona Ana.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Benagil Sea Cave — one of the most famous natural wonders in Portugal. Take a boat tour from Praia de Benagil (approximately 8 km from Lagoa) to access the cathedral-like cave with its dramatic skylight opening. Budget boat tours cost approximately €15–20 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat tour, relax on Praia de Benagil and swim in the turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail east towards Praia do Carvalho — a hidden beach accessible only through a tunnel carved through the cliff (free and spectacular).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a quiet evening. Visit the local Lagoa farmers market if running (check local schedule) or browse the town's small shops for local ceramics, azulejos tiles, and Algarve honey.

meals.breakfast: Local café in Lagoa — galão and fresh pastry — approx €3.50
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia de Benagil — grilled sardine sandwich and local beer — approx €9
meals.dinner: Self-catering at accommodation — fresh seafood from the local market cooked simply, with local wine — approx €15 for two

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil boat tour in advance, especially in September when tours can still be busy. Alternatively, strong swimmers can kayak into the cave independently — kayak rentals are available at the beach for approximately €15 per person. Do not attempt to swim into the cave from outside without experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Albufeira (approximately 20 km east of Lagoa). Explore the old town — the whitewashed streets, the tunnel to the main beach, and the lively fish market area. Visit the Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) at the heart of the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a walk to Praia da Oura or Praia do Peneco — quieter beaches just east of the old town. Alternatively, join an affordable jeep safari tour departing from Albufeira that explores the Algarve hinterland, visiting traditional villages and cork oak forests (approx €30–35 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Albufeira's famous sunset from the clifftop miradouro (viewpoint) overlooking the old town beach. Have dinner in the old town before catching the bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa before departure — coffee and croissant — approx €3
meals.lunch: Tasca in Albufeira old town — prato do dia with soup and dessert — approx €10
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant in Albufeira old town — grilled dourada (sea bream) with salad and house wine — approx €14–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Lagoa to Albufeira takes approximately 30 minutes and costs €3 each way. Albufeira can be very touristy in the old town strip — venture a few streets back from the main tourist drag for more authentic and affordable dining options.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favourite beach from the trip or discover Praia de Porto de Mós near Lagos for something new. This long, relatively uncrowded beach is backed by dramatic cliffs and is perfect for a final swim in the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monchique mountains (approximately 35 km north of Lagoa) for a scenic afternoon escape from the coast. Explore the spa town of Caldas de Monchique — a charming thermal spa village nestled in the eucalyptus and cork oak forests. Sample the famous Monchique medronho brandy at a local distillery.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Algarve — return to Lagoa for a special farewell dinner. Treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent meal at a local restaurant, toasting the trip with a bottle of the best local Algarve wine you discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Local café in Lagoa — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto ham, and coffee — approx €6
meals.lunch: Traditional restaurant in Caldas de Monchique — local mountain cuisine, roast pork and chestnuts — approx €12
meals.dinner: Best local restaurant in Lagoa — cataplana de marisco (mixed seafood cataplana) — approx €18–22 per person as a farewell splurge

day_by_day.notes: Bus to Monchique from Portimão takes approximately 45 minutes. Take the bus from Lagoa to Portimão first (€2.50), then connect to Monchique (€3.50). The Algarve cataplana is the region's signature dish — a copper pot seafood stew that is a must-try before leaving.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagoa — take a slow farewell walk around Lagoa town. Visit the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (parish church) with its beautiful blue and white azulejo tile façade. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — local wine, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), fig and almond confections, and local ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Lagoa Boutique Stay and arrange transfer to Faro Airport. Allow at least 1.5 hours travel time from Lagoa to Faro Airport. Spend any remaining time in Faro old town (Cidade Velha) if your flight allows — explore the Roman walls and the Igreja dos Ossos (Chapel of Bones).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at a Lagoa café — pastel de nata, fresh orange juice, and bica coffee — approx €4
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the airport — approx €8–10
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — budget accordingly

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Lagoa to Faro Airport: take the Eva Bus from Lagoa to Faro (approx €5, 50 minutes) then airport shuttle or taxi (€5–8). Total budget summary estimate for 13 days per person: Accommodation (12 nights at budget boutique): €400–600; Food and drink: €250–350; Transport: €80–120; Activities and entrance fees: €100–150; Wine tastings: €60–80; Miscellaneous and souvenirs: €50–80. Total estimated budget: €940–1,380 per person for the full 13-day trip.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Faro Airport to Lagoa Boutique Stay (~30 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll through Lagoa town center to get your bearings. Visit the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (Parish Church) and explore the charming main square.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening — walk along the local streets of Lagoa, browse the small shops, and settle into the pace of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Snack on the plane or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at a café near the airport before transfer
meals.lunch: Light bite at a café in Lagoa town center upon arrival — try Café Central for a prego sandwich and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Forno in Lagoa — a welcoming mid-range spot serving traditional Algarvian grilled fish and cataplana. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pick up a local SIM card or confirm data roaming. Ask the hotel for a map and their top restaurant recommendations. September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) and sunny — perfect beach weather.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most picturesque beaches in the Algarve (~10 min from Lagoa). Arrive early to claim a spot on the golden sand, swim in the clear Atlantic waters, and explore the dramatic rock formations along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Algar Seco boardwalk — a stunning coastal path with sea caves, arches, and natural rock pools carved by the ocean. Just east of Carvoeiro, free to access. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar, then enjoy dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a local pastelaria in Lagoa — fresh bread, ham, cheese, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a light lunch at a beach café at Praia de Carvoeiro — grilled sardine sandwich or salad (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — beloved local spot for fresh seafood, grilled sea bass, and local wines. ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Algar Seco walk. Parking is available near Carvoeiro beach. Alternatively, take a local taxi (~€8–10 each way) or rent a car from the hotel area for the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning at Adega do Cantor (Winery of the Singer) near Guia, just 15 min from Lagoa. This acclaimed winery, co-founded by Sir Cliff Richard, produces excellent Algarve wines. Book a guided tour and tasting in advance (~€15–20 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Silves (~15 min from Lagoa) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) and wander the historic medina streets below.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Silves for dinner, enjoying the atmospheric old town at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, bread, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Silves after the castle visit — try Café Inglês, a charming spot built into the castle walls serving salads and light dishes (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — legendary seafood restaurant known for its cataplana and shellfish. ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Adega do Cantor wine tour in advance online. Silves is easily drivable from Lagoa. The castle is open daily; September crowds are lighter than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Praia da Marinha (~15 min from Lagoa), consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim, snorkel, or simply admire the towering golden limestone cliffs. Arrive by 9:00 to secure parking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat cave tour departing from Praia da Marinha or nearby Benagil — explore the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil), one of the most photographed natural wonders in Portugal. Book in advance (~€20–25 per person, 1.5 hrs).
day_by_day.evening: Relax back at the hotel. Take a dip in the hotel pool if available, then head out for a quiet dinner in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick coffee and pastry at a local bakery before driving to Marinha
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach or snack bar near Praia da Marinha — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap or fresh fruit (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taberna da Praça in Lagoa — rustic Portuguese tavern with petiscos (Portuguese tapas), local wine, and daily specials. ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil boat tour is extremely popular — book 2–3 days in advance. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it; the waters at Marinha are crystal clear in September. Wear reef shoes as the rocks can be sharp.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip west to Lagos (~25 min from Lagoa). Start with a walk through Lagos old town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the Igreja de Santo António (Church of St. Anthony), a baroque masterpiece with gilded woodwork (€3 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Ponta da Piedade — a breathtaking headland with dramatic sea stacks, grottos, and turquoise lagoons. Take a kayak or small boat tour of the grottoes (~€15–20). Then relax at Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos' most scenic beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos' vibrant evening atmosphere — aperitivo hour on a terrace bar, then dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch in Lagos old town — Restaurante O Camilo near the beach is excellent for fresh fish with a view (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio in Lagos — intimate courtyard restaurant with creative Algarvian cuisine and a good local wine list. ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Park on the outskirts of Lagos and walk in — the old town is pedestrian-friendly. Ponta da Piedade is a 20-min walk from the town center or a short taxi ride. Sunset from the headland is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (~10 min from Lagoa) — a beautiful estate with vineyards, sculpture gardens, and excellent wine. Take a guided vineyard and cellar tour followed by a tasting of 4–5 wines (~€18–25). Booking recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the riverside town of Estômbar and the nearby Arade River. Rent a bike or take a leisurely walk along the river path. Alternatively, visit the local market if it's a market day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Browse the town's wine shops to pick up a bottle of local Algarve wine to enjoy on your hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery's terrace café or picnic in the vineyard grounds with local cheese and charcuterie (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Quatro Águas in Portimão (~20 min) — riverside seafood restaurant with stunning estuary views. Try the grilled dourada (sea bream). ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the Algarve's most scenic wineries and also features large outdoor sculptures — a unique combination. Check their website for current tour times. Great opportunity to purchase bottles to bring home.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Armação de Pêra (~15 min from Lagoa). Visit the long, wide Praia de Armação de Pêra — one of the largest beaches in the Algarve. Morning swim and a walk along the promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip from Armação de Pêra to explore the hidden sea caves and grottos of the Algarvian coastline between Armação and Benagil from a different angle (~€15–20). Alternatively, visit the small 17th-century fort at the end of the beach (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront bar in Armação de Pêra, then dinner in the town.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a café in Lagoa before departure
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a beachfront restaurant in Armação — try Restaurante Estrela do Mar for fresh clams, shrimp, and local wine (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Zé in Armação de Pêra — a beloved local tasca (tavern) with grilled fish, honest prices, and a warm atmosphere. ~€15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day — keep the pace relaxed. September means fewer crowds than July/August but still warm water temperatures (~22°C). This is a great day to simply enjoy the beach without rushing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Portimão (~15 min from Lagoa) — explore the waterfront Ribeira de Portimão, browse the morning fish market, and visit the excellent Museu de Portimão (Museum of Portimão), housed in a former sardine canning factory. €3 entry, fascinating industrial and maritime history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha (~5 min from Portimão) — a long, golden beach backed by rust-red cliffs and a lively promenade. Swim, walk the cliff-top boardwalk, and visit the 16th-century Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the beach's eastern end (free).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Portimão's lively waterfront for dinner — the Ribeira strip is famous for grilled sardines.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines at one of the famous open-air grills along Portimão's Ribeira — this is a quintessential Algarve experience. Lunch for two with wine ~€18–25
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — a well-regarded mid-range restaurant with excellent cataplana de marisco (seafood stew). ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Museu de Portimão is closed on Mondays — check the day of the week. Portimão's Ribeira sardine grills are iconic; the smell of charcoal and sardines wafting over the waterfront is unforgettable. Book dinner in advance if visiting on a weekend.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Sagres (~50 min from Lagoa) — the dramatic southwestern tip of Portugal and Europe. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3), a 15th-century fortress where Henry the Navigator planned his voyages of discovery. Walk the windswept cliffs with panoramic Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 10 min to Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand on the wild, cliff-edged promontory and watch the Atlantic crash against the rocks. Visit the lighthouse (small entry fee). Then relax at Praia do Beliche, a sheltered beach below the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagoa, stopping in Portimão or Lagos for dinner if desired, or return to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the drive
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sagres village — Restaurante A Tasca in Sagres for fresh tuna steak (atum) — tuna is the local specialty here. ~€16–22 per person
meals.dinner: Dinner back in Lagoa or en route — Restaurante O Forno in Lagoa for a comforting end to a long day. ~€20–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the furthest point from Lagoa in this itinerary — allow a full day. The wind at Cabo de São Vicente can be fierce even in September; bring a light jacket. This is one of the most atmospheric and historically significant spots in Portugal — not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, and spend the morning at leisure. Take a yoga session, read by the pool, or explore Lagoa's local market (check market day schedule with the hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lagoa Wine Cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa) — one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve, located right in Lagoa town. Take a self-guided or short guided tour and taste the local Algarvian wines including the distinctive Lagoa DOC whites. Very affordable (~€5–10 for tasting).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Lagoa town, visit the small local shops and artisan stores, and enjoy a relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Long, leisurely breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Lagoa — a local café or tasca for a prato do dia (dish of the day), typically €8–12 including bread, salad, and a drink
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Barão in Lagoa — a reliable mid-range local restaurant with a full menu of grilled meats and fish, good house wine. ~€18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day mid-trip. The Lagoa Wine Cooperative is a hidden gem that many tourists overlook — the wines here are excellent value and the staff are knowledgeable and welcoming. Stock up on bottles to enjoy during your remaining evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Albufeira (~20 min from Lagoa). Explore the old town (Albufeira Velha) — wander the whitewashed streets, visit the clifftop miradouro (viewpoint) overlooking Praia dos Pescadores, and browse the local shops and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Praia de São Rafael (~5 min from Albufeira) — a stunning small beach framed by golden rock arches and sea stacks. Swim, snorkel, or take a paddleboard lesson (~€15–20/hr). Less crowded than the main Albufeira beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Albufeira old town for the evening — the pedestrian streets come alive at sunset with street musicians, artisan stalls, and a buzzing restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch at a clifftop restaurant in Albufeira old town — Restaurante A Ruína is a classic, perched on the cliff above the beach with excellent fresh fish. ~€22–30 per person
meals.dinner: Dinner in Albufeira old town — Tasca do Viegas for traditional Algarvian dishes in a cozy setting, good local wine selection. ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be touristy but the old town retains genuine charm. Avoid the 'Strip' area (Avenida Sá Carneiro) which is geared toward package tourism. Stick to the old town and nearby beaches for an authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine experience — visit Herdade dos Pimenteiros or another boutique winery in the Lagoa/Silves area for a morning tasting and vineyard walk. Alternatively, revisit a favorite beach for a last long morning swim and sunbathe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Silves for a final afternoon — climb back up to the castle for golden hour light photography, visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2), and browse the artisan ceramic shops along the cobbled streets. Pick up handmade azulejo tiles or local pottery as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Silves — a local tasca for soup and bread, keeping appetite for the farewell dinner (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurante Veneza in Portimão or O Barradas in Silves — both offer refined Algarvian cuisine with excellent wine pairings. Budget €30–40 per person for a special occasion.

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon in Silves to buy last-minute gifts — the ceramic shops here are excellent and prices are fair. Consider buying a bottle or two of Algarvian wine from the cooperative or a winery to bring home. Check baggage weight limits for wine transport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve — wake up early for one last sunrise walk or a quick dip at the nearest beach. Pack and check out of the hotel. Drive a short scenic route through the Lagoa countryside if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport (~30 min from Lagoa). Allow 2 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for last-minute Portuguese wine, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), or fleur de sel from the Algarve salt pans.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, culture, and Algarvian sunshine.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — savor the last pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop at a café en route to Faro — toasted sandwich and juice (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the hotel. Leave extra time for the airport transfer in case of traffic. Faro Airport is small but can get busy; arrive at least 90 minutes before departure. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Lagoa Boutique Stay and settle into your suite. Enjoy a welcome drink and property orientation. Take a leisurely stroll through the charming village of Lagoa, exploring its whitewashed streets and the 18th-century Igreja Matriz de Lagoa.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel's pool or spa to recover from travel. Enjoy a curated welcome dinner at the hotel or a nearby upscale restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments upon arrival at the hotel — charcuterie board, local cheeses, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — renowned for fresh seafood and Algarvian cuisine with stunning estuary views

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Adega do Cantor winery (formerly owned by Cliff Richard) near Guia, just minutes from Lagoa. Enjoy a premium guided cellar tour and vertical tasting of their award-winning Algarvian wines, including the flagship Vida Nova rosé.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the Algarve's most picturesque beaches. Rent a private sun lounger and parasol at a premium beach club. Explore the dramatic limestone cliffs and sea caves by kayak or paddleboard.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the cliffside bar overlooking Carvoeiro village. Dinner at a top-rated restaurant in Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel — pastéis de nata, fresh fruit, artisan breads, local honey, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish and seafood at Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro with panoramic ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant (Michelin-starred) in Carvoeiro — contemporary Algarvian tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Bon Bon Restaurant well in advance — it is one of the Algarve's most sought-after fine dining experiences. Carvoeiro is approximately 10 minutes from Lagoa.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided wine tour of the Lagoa wine region — visit the historic Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, one of Portugal's oldest cooperatives, for an in-depth tasting of regional Negra Mole and Crato Branco varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the coastal village of Ferragudo on foot — visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade, browse artisan shops, and discover hidden beaches like Praia de Angrinha. Optional private boat charter along the Arade River.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Arade River estuary with champagne and canapés, watching the sun dip behind Portimão's skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with local specialties including almond pastries and fresh-squeezed orange juice from Algarve groves
meals.lunch: Tapas and wine at a traditional tasca in Ferragudo village
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante A Tasca in Ferragudo — intimate family-run restaurant celebrated for its cataplana de marisco (seafood stew)

day_by_day.notes: The Arade River sunset cruise typically runs 1.5–2 hours. Pre-book with a local charter company. Ferragudo is 5 minutes from Lagoa.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — visit the magnificent Moorish Castelo de Silves, a UNESCO-listed red sandstone fortress offering sweeping views over the Arade Valley. Explore the Silves Cathedral and the medieval old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Quinta dos Vales estate winery near Estômbar — one of the Algarve's most acclaimed boutique wineries. Enjoy a premium tasting of their sculpture garden wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Visit the rooftop terrace bar of a boutique hotel in Lagoa for aperitivos before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with seasonal Algarvian fruits and freshly baked breads
meals.lunch: Lunch at Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary seafood restaurant famous for its cataplana and grilled tiger prawns
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande — a refined countryside restaurant in a historic quinta with a renowned Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 15 minutes from Lagoa. Quinta dos Vales tastings should be reserved in advance. Vila Lisa is a short 20-minute drive and is considered one of the Algarve's finest dining institutions.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat excursion from Portimão Marina to the spectacular Benagil Sea Cave — one of the world's most beautiful sea caves. Explore the hidden beaches and dramatic grottos of the Algarve coastline by private boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia da Marinha, consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. Enjoy a premium beach club experience with butler service, chilled towels, and curated snack platters.
day_by_day.evening: Spa evening at the hotel — book a signature Portuguese massage using local argan and almond oils, followed by time in the steam room and jacuzzi.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivered to your suite — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the hotel, enjoyed on Praia da Marinha — including lobster rolls, chilled rosé, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ocean Restaurant (two Michelin stars) at Vila Vita Parc in Porches — one of Portugal's most celebrated fine dining experiences with an extraordinary wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book Ocean Restaurant months in advance — it is among the most prestigious restaurants in Portugal. Praia da Marinha is 10 minutes from Lagoa. Vila Vita Parc is 15 minutes away.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) — a fascinating converted sardine canning factory now housing exhibits on the region's maritime and archaeological heritage. Stroll along the Portimão waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia da Rocha beach afternoon — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches with golden sands and dramatic rock formations. Enjoy a VIP sun lounger setup at a premium beach club with cocktail service.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's vibrant marina district. Visit the famous Portimão sardine festival area and enjoy the lively atmosphere of the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with local specialties
meals.lunch: Lunch at Taberna da Maré in Portimão — contemporary Portuguese cuisine with a focus on locally caught fish and regional ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Buzio Restaurant at Bela Vista Hotel & Spa in Portimão — elegant beachfront dining with panoramic Atlantic views and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is 10 minutes from Lagoa. Praia da Rocha is adjacent to Portimão. September weather is typically warm and sunny — perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Alvor village — a beautifully preserved fishing village with a 16th-century Manueline church, labyrinthine Moorish alleyways, and a stunning lagoon boardwalk through the Alvor Estuary Nature Reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia de Alvor beach afternoon — a sweeping 4km beach with calm, shallow waters ideal for swimming. Arrange a private catamaran sailing trip along the coastline with onboard champagne service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Alvor beach, followed by a leisurely drive back to Lagoa. Quiet evening at the hotel with a curated in-room wine and cheese selection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Restaurante Três Palmeiras in Alvor — a legendary institution overlooking the lagoon, famous for its lobster and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner experience at the hotel or a rented quinta — a curated 5-course menu featuring Algarvian ingredients paired with regional wines

day_by_day.notes: Alvor is approximately 20 minutes from Lagoa. The Alvor Estuary boardwalk is a must — bring comfortable walking shoes. Pre-arrange the private chef experience through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the wild and dramatic Costa Vicentina — the western Algarve's unspoiled Atlantic coastline. Begin with a scenic drive to Sagres, stopping at the iconic Cabo de São Vicente (Cape St. Vincent), the southwesternmost point of continental Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fortaleza de Sagres — a historic 15th-century fortress steeped in the Age of Discovery. Walk the dramatic clifftops and watch Atlantic waves crash below. Visit the famous wind compass (rosa dos ventos) carved into the ground.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagoa via the scenic EN125. Stop at a viewpoint for the last light of the day before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast to prepare for the day trip
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Memmo Baleeira in Sagres — stylish waterfront restaurant with fresh catch-of-the-day and panoramic harbor views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Leão in Lagos — celebrated for its traditional Algarvian dishes and extensive Portuguese wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour from Lagoa. The drive along the west coast is spectacular. Bring a light jacket as Cabo de São Vicente can be windy. Lagos is a convenient stop on the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos — one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Visit the Ponta da Piedade sea stacks and grottos by private boat or kayak — among the most dramatic coastal formations in Portugal. Walk the old town walls and visit the Igreja de Santo António.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium wine experience at Quinta da Penina or another Lagos-area estate. Alternatively, visit the Lagos Farmers Market for artisan producers, local honey, and Algarvian medronho brandy tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a rooftop bar in Lagos old town with views over the Atlantic. Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere of Lagos before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at No Patio in Lagos — a sophisticated courtyard restaurant known for its creative Portuguese cuisine and natural wine selection
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vistas Restaurant at Monte Santo Resort — Michelin-recommended with panoramic views and an outstanding tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is 20 minutes from Lagoa. Ponta da Piedade boat tours depart from Lagos Marina — book in advance. September is ideal for calm sea conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated spa and wellness morning at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa resort. Enjoy treatments such as a hot stone massage, facial, and hydrotherapy circuit. Take a gentle yoga or meditation session by the pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Praia de Carvoeiro for a leisurely afternoon. Explore the Algar Seco rock formations — a stunning natural sculpture of amber limestone arches, grottoes, and sea pools accessible by a short clifftop walk.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo hour on the hotel terrace. Dress for a special evening out.

meals.breakfast: Light in-room breakfast — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, granola, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled seabass, garden salad, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Return visit to Bon Bon (or alternative Michelin experience) — alternatively, dinner at Henrique Leis Restaurant in Almancil for a celebrated Alsatian-Portuguese fusion tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: A dedicated rest day is important mid-trip. Algar Seco is a short walk from Carvoeiro beach and is best visited in the late afternoon light. Henrique Leis is 45 minutes from Lagoa but worth the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Excursion to Loulé — the Algarve's cultural heartland. Visit the spectacular Moorish-style Loulé Market, one of the finest covered markets in Portugal, overflowing with local produce, spices, ceramics, and fresh seafood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Golden Triangle — the ultra-premium resort area encompassing Vale do Lobo, Quinta do Lago, and Vilamoura. Explore the luxury marina at Vilamoura and the pristine beaches of Quinta do Lago.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at the Vilamoura Marina's premium waterfront bars. Enjoy the glamorous atmosphere of one of Europe's finest marinas.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Loulé Jardim Hotel Restaurant or a gourmet café near the market — featuring market-fresh ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Gusto by Heinz Beck at Conrad Algarve in Quinta do Lago — a Michelin-starred restaurant helmed by one of Europe's most celebrated chefs

day_by_day.notes: Loulé is approximately 40 minutes from Lagoa. Quinta do Lago is 45 minutes away. Gusto by Heinz Beck requires advance reservations. This is a longer driving day — consider hiring a private driver.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach of the trip (Praia da Marinha or Carvoeiro recommended). Arrange a premium beach setup with a private attendant, chilled beverages, and a curated snack selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last wine tasting experience — visit a final local producer for a farewell tasting. Consider visiting Quinta da Franceza near Lagoa for their organic wines and beautiful vineyard setting. Purchase bottles to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip — a celebration of 13 days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time and savor every detail
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium beach club — fresh oysters, grilled octopus, and chilled Algarvian white wine
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Ocean Restaurant (Vila Vita Parc) or a return to your favorite dining experience of the trip — with a special wine pairing selected by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to purchase last-minute gifts — local wines, almond products, handmade ceramics, and artisan preserves make excellent souvenirs. Pack purchased wine carefully for the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagoa — enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow walk through Lagoa town, visit the local café for a final bica (espresso) and pastel de nata. Check out of the hotel and arrange private luxury transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Arrive with ample time for check-in and security. Browse the airport's duty-free for last-minute Portuguese wines, ginjinha liqueur, and pastéis de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through the Algarve's finest beaches, wines, and culinary experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final full hotel breakfast — indulge in all your favorites from the past two weeks
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel before departure or at Faro Airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out from the hotel if your flight departs in the afternoon — most luxury properties accommodate this with advance notice. Faro Airport is approximately 40 minutes from Lagoa. Allow 2.5 hours before departure for international flights.
